changes: p1 Bhāsurānandanātha: role 'teacher' → 'other' (he is the author's guru, not involved in producing this copy); noted identity with Bhāskararāya

p4 Gaṇeśa: confidence high → medium; the colophon has two instrumentals with one 'likhitaṃ', so co-scribe is one reading, but owner (gaṇeśasūriṇā for -ṇaḥ) is also possible; the catalogue names only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa
p7 Rājābhāū: 'Kive' moved from affiliation to titles as a surname (upanāmaka); evidence trimmed
notes expanded: umanāmakasya = upanāmakasya; smṛtīyaḥ(!) probably = tṛtīyaḥ; dhuṃḍhirājātmaka- = -ātmaja-

persons.name: Rājābhāū
persons.evidence: kive ity umanāmakasya(!) rājābhāu yasya gṛhe

notes: The text is Umānandanātha's Nityotsava. Bhāsurānandanātha is the initiatory name of Bhāskararāya, the author's guru; he had no part in this copy. 'mānasenomānaṃdanāthena' = mānasena + umānandanāthena. 'yauvanollāsasmṛtīyaḥ (!)' probably stands for 'yauvanollāsas tṛtīyaḥ'. 'umanāmakasya(!)' = upanāmakasya, so Kive (Kibe) is Rājābhāū's surname; the Kibe family was prominent in Indore. 'dhuṃḍhirājātmaka-' stands for -ātmaja-. Two people stand in the instrumental (Gaṇeśasūri, son of Dhuṇḍhirāja, surname Devasthalī, and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, son of Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa) before a single 'likhitaṃ'. Their fathers differ, so they are two people. Gaṇeśa could be a co-scribe. Or 'gaṇeśasūriṇā' may be a slip for the genitive '-ṇaḥ', which would make him the owner of the book. The catalogue lists only Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa as scribe. No date is given.
